decisions.decision: A single ticket with a malformed stored `due` prevents the service from starting and the error names the offending record, even with due times switched off.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the service to keep serving the old API while operators repair the affected deadline.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-6 lines 43–46 and R-7 line 52

decisions.decision: An explicitly empty `DUE_HOURS_*` setting selects the built-in default for that priority.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted an explicitly blank setting to stop startup so a configuration mistake cannot permanently assign tickets the wrong deadline.

decisions.decision: The production rollout relies on operators to deploy with `DUE_TIMES` off, confirm the data file contains due times, and then switch it on.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted startup to enforce the rollout sequence by refusing `DUE_TIMES=on` if the file still needs backfilling.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-10 line 71 and R-6 line 43

decisions.decision: With `overdue=true` and both status and priority specified, an overdue ticket qualifies if it matches either of those two filters.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected an overdue search to require all three conditions, as the current API documentation already says for status and priority together.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-5 line 39, and repo/docs/api.md, List tickets lines 69–77

decisions.decision: The creation audit entry omits the deadline assigned to a new ticket.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the audit history to record the original promise so it can be recovered later.

decisions.decision: The operator CLI and weekly report keep their existing output in both switch modes.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted a deadline in the CLI's human-readable output and overdue counts in the weekly report while preserving the existing raw columns.
decisions.where: record/01-intake.md, Q6 lines 114–121, and repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-6 line 48 and R-7 line 52

decisions.decision: Overdue results keep the usual cursor pagination and ticket ID order.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the earliest deadlines first so agents see the longest-overdue tickets on the first page.

decisions.decision: The ticket receipt notification keeps its current content and omits the due time.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the receipt to tell the person who filed the ticket when to expect a response.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-1 line 11, and repo/docs/api.md, Create a ticket lines 64–65

decisions.decision: Backfilling a ticket's deadline leaves the ticket's `updated` timestamp unchanged.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the backfill to advance `updated` so consumers that look for changed tickets can pick up the new field.

decisions.decision: A ticket request body containing `due` is rejected with HTTP 400 as an unknown field.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the API to ignore the read-only field so clients can echo back a ticket body without stripping `due`.

decisions.decision: The API returns `due` as an ISO 8601 UTC string in the same format as `created`.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted a numeric Unix timestamp for deadline comparisons in their clients.
decisions.where: record/01-intake.md, Q9 lines 141–148, and repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-1 line 8

decisions.decision: The work designates the release as version 1.5.0.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the feature shipped in the 1.4 maintenance line as 1.4.1 because the API defaults to its existing behavior.
